<!--
NUMBER PENDING. The Figure 4 supplements are being rebuilt on the five-member plane and the
numbering is settled once the set is known; the ones written against the superseded figure are
parked in `../in_progress/figure_4_supplements_20260731/`. File name carries the content until
then.

WHAT IT IS. Figure 4's second moment, factored. Same plane, same rows, same members, same scale,
same two line families, same everything: the only thing that changes is what the top bar says.
Where Figure 4 nests moment > member > parameter, this nests COMPONENT > member > parameter, so a
reader who has paid for Figure 4 reads this one with no new instructions. 18 columns, the same as
the body figure, so the geometry and `per_row` are the same too.

THE TWO COMPONENTS. The Gaussian information distortion factors into two congruences that the
battery computes separately:

  PER-SAMPLE     G^-1/2 J_sample G^-1/2, the departure of a SINGLE interval from the Gaussian the
                 algorithm assumes: the skewness and kurtosis of the one-step residual. It is
                 the price of the closure, and it must go to 1 as the channel count grows, since
                 that is when the binomial occupancy becomes normal.
  CORRELATION    J_sample^-1/2 J J_sample^-1/2, the temporal memory ACROSS intervals that a
                 likelihood diagonal in time cannot see. It is the price of the factorisation,
                 and nothing about the channel count makes it go away.

Both are factors with a null of 1, so they take Figure 4's palette and Figure 4's two criteria
unchanged, and both are read at theta_pool from battery_pool_G, the same anchor as Figure 4's B.

THE PRODUCT IS NOT EXACT PER PARAMETER, and the caption has to say so. Total = sample x
correlation holds exactly in log-det, and it is what makes the whole-matrix maps safe; per
parameter the reconstruction is K CDM K^T with K = H^-1/2 J_s^1/2, NOT SDM^1/2 CDM SDM^1/2, so
the diagonal of the product is not the product of the diagonals. Reading a cell of Figure 4's B
as the product of the two cells here is right to within that rotation and no further. It is close
in practice (R at N_ch 1e3: 1.024 x 1.433 = 1.468 against a total of 1.481) and it is not an
identity.

WHAT IT SHOWS, measured at noise 0.1, medians over the seven intervals:

                        N_ch:     10      100     1000    10000
    per-sample, k_off   LSE      1.016   0.967   0.943   0.947
                        NR       1.239   1.019   5.676  47.165
                        INR      1.724   1.154   1.015   1.003
                        R        1.086   1.071   1.024   0.998
                        IR       1.099   1.068   1.038   1.007
    per-sample, N_ch    NR       1.191   1.207  11.569 569.391
                        INR      1.079   1.048   1.010   1.001
                        R        0.906   0.926   0.933   0.960
                        IR       0.913   0.962   0.972   0.986
    correlation, k_off  LSE     10.818  13.698  14.155  14.073
                        NR      16.513  19.467  21.162  21.194
                        INR     16.487  20.713  21.778  22.103
                        R        1.354   1.356   1.433   1.471
                        IR       1.239   1.019   1.017   1.000
    correlation, N_ch   NR       8.776   8.970   6.278   5.475
                        INR      9.095  10.300   9.887  10.169
                        R        0.994   1.255   1.342   1.338
                        IR       0.914   0.967   0.995   0.997

Three readings, and the first is the one this supplement exists for.

  1. NR AND INR HAVE THE SAME CORRELATION PART. 16.5 / 19.5 / 21.2 / 21.2 against 16.5 / 20.7 /
     21.8 / 22.1 on k_off: the same open-loop temporal structure, as it must be, since the two
     differ by a per-sample variance term and not by anything about time. What separates them is
     the SAMPLE part, and there the split is total: NR runs 1.24, 1.02, 5.68, 47.2 and diverges,
     INR runs 1.72, 1.15, 1.02, 1.00 and converges to one. In the channel-number direction it is
     starker still, 569 against 1.00. So the divergence Figure 4 shows for NR is not a temporal
     failure at all: it is the one-interval variance being wrong by a term that grows with the
     channel count, which is exactly what the omitted N*ms is.
  2. THE RECURSION BUYS THE OTHER FACTOR AND ONLY THE OTHER FACTOR. INR to IR takes the
     correlation part from 22.1 to 1.000 and leaves the sample part where it already was (1.003
     against 1.007). R to IR is the same statement one rung lower, 1.47 to 1.00.
  3. LEAST SQUARES IS PER-SAMPLE HONEST AND TEMPORALLY BLIND: sample 0.95 to 1.02 across four
     decades, correlation 10.8 to 14.1. Its failure is entirely the factorisation, which is worth
     stating plainly because it is the concession the paper makes to the classical fit.

Read together with Figure 4 the ladder becomes a 2x2 with a mechanism attached: the interval
term fixes the per-sample factor, the recursion fixes the correlation factor, and calibration
needs both.

INR IS ONE NOISE LEVEL SO FAR, so its two columns are the tiles the layout draws for a member
under `MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS`, at noise 0.1 only. They become contours on their own once the sweep
lands. Everything else on this plane has its full staircase.

SUPERSEDES, when the numbering is settled, `figure_4_supplement_3.Rmd` (the map version of the
same split, written for R against IR and never built) and `figure_4_supplement_4.Rmd` (the line
version, which carries the same decomposition against N_ch resolved by noise). Both are parked in
`../in_progress/`. The line version says something this one does not, namely how the split moves
with noise as a continuous cut, so it is a candidate to keep rather than a certainty to drop.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# The same roster as the body figure, and for the same reason: this is Figure 4's own second
# moment taken apart, so any member missing here would be a member whose mechanism is not shown.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR", "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "LSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
                    macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# `stat` already carries all three components (COMPS in figure_4_common.R) with a `comp` column,
# and Figure 4 filters it to "total". Here the two halves take the two factors instead. Same
# readout as Figure 4's B, log10 of the CI-aware Dconf, so a cell means the same thing in all
# three files: the factor by which the reported second moment is wrong.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "per-sample distortion", letter = "A",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "sample"), zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)),
  list(lab = "temporal-correlation distortion", letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "corr"),   zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 5.95}
# 18 columns, the same as Figure 4, so the same nominal knob: 0.179, measured at x 0.1567,
# y 0.1562, 99.7 per cent isotropic (tmp/calib_fig4.R, tmp/measure_fig4.py).
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.179, out = "Figure_4_supplement_sample_corr.pdf",
            cb_title = "factor by which\nthe report is wrong")
```
